questions.why: ZDR covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs only. Batch, Files, Skills, code execution and the MCP connector are excluded, and Covered Models (Fable 5, Mythos 5) require 30-day retention.

questions.q: A customer requires EU data residency. What does the guide say the real procurement decision is?

options.text: Set the anthropic-client-geo header on claude.ai Enterprise
Claude via AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex EU regions — EU residency is not offered on first-party surfaces
Request an EU workspace from the Anthropic account team
Enable ZDR, which removes the residency question

questions.why: First-party surfaces default to US infrastructure and offer no EU residency; the EU path runs through the cloud providers under their DPA/BAA.

questions.q: What is the spend-control difference between self-serve and sales-assisted Enterprise?

options.text: Both stop automatically when the budget is reached
Self-serve stops org-wide when the prepaid pool hits zero; sales-assisted invoicing has no automatic stop, so limits must be set explicitly
Sales-assisted caps usage at 120% of forecast by default

questions.why: The prepaid pool is a built-in circuit breaker. On invoicing there is none — you can overrun unless you configure limits.

questions.q: Which cost lever gives a 50% discount but is excluded from ZDR scope?
questions.why: Route non-urgent API jobs to Batch for half price — but a ZDR workspace cannot use it.

questions.q: What benchmark does the guide give for Claude Code spend when setting engineering-group limits?
questions.why: About $13/developer/day is the industry-average burn cited as a useful starting point for group-level limits.

questions.q: Which plans can use Projects, and what happens when project knowledge outgrows the context window?

options.text: All plans including Free; extra files are silently dropped
Pro and above; retrieval (RAG) mode expands effective capacity up to ~10×
Enterprise only; the project must be split manually
All paid plans; the oldest files are evicted first

questions.why: Projects are not on Free. They carry a 200K-token window (500K on Enterprise), and RAG mode kicks in automatically as knowledge approaches the limit.

questions.q: How does Claude handle PDFs of different lengths?

options.text: Every PDF gets full vision plus text analysis
≤100 pages: vision + text; 101–1000 pages: text only; over 1000 pages: rejected
≤100 pages: text only; anything longer needs the Files API
PDFs are always converted to plain text before analysis

questions.why: The 100-page vision cutoff is one of the capability boundaries that trips users far more often than prompting skill does.

questions.q: What is the default sandbox network posture for code execution?

options.text: On everywhere with unrestricted internet access
On by default for Free/Pro/Max but limited to approved domains; off by default on Team/Enterprise
On for Team/Enterprise only, since they are the governed tiers

questions.why: Consumer tiers get approved-domain access (pypi, npm, github, crates.io, Ubuntu archives, api.anthropic.com); the governed tiers start closed.

questions.q: What is the runtime requirement for a Cowork Scheduled Task?

options.text: Nothing — it runs in Anthropic's cloud
The computer must be awake with the desktop app open; missed runs re-fire when you reopen it
The mobile app must be installed and signed in
A connector must be marked Always allow

questions.why: That runtime dependency is the main reason to rebuild a briefing as a cloud Claude Code Routine instead.

questions.q: What are the documented daily caps on Claude Code Routines (Research Preview, as of August 2026)?

options.text: 25 per day on every paid plan
Unlimited, bounded only by spend limits

questions.why: Research Preview limits change — the guide flags these caps for re-verification before you design around them.

questions.q: What can the Gmail connector NOT do?
questions.why: Gmail through the connector is draft-only — an example of Layer 3, tool design, bounding what a connector exposes.

questions.q: The compute/governance gradient says to match each use case against which three variables?

options.text: Team size, budget, and vendor preference
Task type, context size, and governance needs

questions.why: Start with low-risk, high-volume workflows, prove value, then escalate to governed, high-context use cases.

questions.q: What is the hard boundary designers need to know about Claude's visual output?

options.text: It has no native raster image generation — it produces SVG and code-based visuals only

questions.why: Claude analyzes images and generates SVG/HTML/React/Mermaid, but it does not generate photos or bitmap art.

questions.q: What is Anthropic's recommended hybrid context strategy for Claude Code on a large repo?

options.text: Paste the whole codebase into the prompt once per session
Anchor with a CLAUDE.md loaded up front, then retrieve everything else just-in-time with glob/grep
Rely entirely on retrieval and skip CLAUDE.md
Keep one long-running session so context accumulates

questions.why: Standing context up front, everything else pulled on demand — the same principle behind the just-in-time data-analysis pattern.

questions.q: What does the guide call non-negotiable when reviewing contracts with Claude?

options.text: Running on Opus 5 rather than Sonnet 5
Quoting the relevant clauses first, then analyzing them

questions.why: Quote-first grounding is Anthropic's documented anti-hallucination technique for long documents: "Do not summarize clauses you did not quote."

questions.q: What is the finance-workflow rule of thumb about Claude and arithmetic?

options.text: Treat all Claude arithmetic as reliable — it uses a calculator internally
Treat arithmetic-through-code as reliable and mental arithmetic as not
Never let Claude near financial figures
Round every figure to avoid precision errors

questions.why: Ask for the reconciliation logic and totals before trusting output; every figure should arrive with the code that computed it.

questions.q: How should marketing style guidance be phrased in a prompt?

options.text: As a long list of prohibitions so nothing goes off-brand
As what Claude should do, anchored by 3–5 diverse exemplar assets
As a single adjective, to leave room for creativity
As a scoring rubric only, with no examples

questions.why: Tell Claude what TO do; curated few-shot examples steer voice far better than an accumulating laundry list of rules.

questions.q: Which single instruction does the guide call the highest-value line in support prompting?

options.text: "If the article doesn't cover it, say so and draft an escalation instead of improvising."
"Cite the customer's ticket ID in every reply."

questions.why: It converts hallucination risk into a clean escalation — the difference between a wrong answer and a routed one.

questions.q: What should sales teams know about connector write actions in HubSpot?

options.text: They are logged as system actions with no user attribution
They appear in HubSpot's audit log attributed to the user, so treat them as your own edits
They bypass HubSpot permissions since Claude uses a service account
They cannot be audited at all

questions.why: The connector also respects your CRM permissions — Claude never sees records you couldn't see yourself — so gate writes behind approval.

questions.q: What is the consulting-workflow rule about client context?

options.text: Keep one Project for all clients so patterns transfer
One Project per engagement — never mix client Projects
Store client data in chat scrollback rather than Projects
Publish client artifacts so the team can remix them

questions.why: Knowledge isolation keeps client contexts separated; publishing client-confidential artifacts is the matching mistake to avoid.

questions.q: How does the guide distinguish a workflow from an agent?

options.text: Workflows use tools; agents do not
Workflows orchestrate LLMs through predefined code paths; agents dynamically direct their own process and tool use
Workflows run in the cloud; agents run locally
Workflows are single-model; agents are always multi-model

questions.why: Anthropic's compact definition of an agent: "LLMs autonomously using tools in a loop."

questions.q: Which pattern fits a task whose subtasks cannot be predicted in advance?
questions.why: A central LLM breaks the task down at runtime, delegates to workers, and synthesizes — which is literally how Research is built.

questions.q: What is the opening advice of "Building effective agents" that the guide calls its most important sentence?

options.text: Prefer orchestrator-workers as the default architecture
Find the simplest solution possible and only add complexity when needed — which might mean not building agentic systems at all
Use the largest model you can afford

questions.why: Every pattern adds capability and cost, latency, and failure modes. Graduate to one only with a measured reason.

questions.q: Anthropic's multi-agent research system scored +90.2% over single-agent on its internal eval. What is the matching cost fact?

options.text: It uses roughly 15× the tokens of ordinary chat
It uses roughly the same tokens, spread across agents
It costs 50% less because subagents run on Haiku
Token usage explains almost none of the performance variance

questions.why: Agents generally run ~4× chat tokens and multi-agent research ~15×, with token usage explaining 80% of performance variance — so don't spend it on a single-fact lookup.

questions.q: How should a 20k+ token prompt be ordered?

options.text: Query first, then documents, so intent frames the reading
Long documents at the top, the query at the end

questions.why: Anthropic measured up to ~30% quality improvement from putting documents first and the question last.

questions.q: You have corrected Claude Code three times on the same task and it is still off. What does the guide say to do?

options.text: Keep correcting — each pass narrows the error
Switch to a larger model and continue in the same session
Clear and restart with a more specific prompt
Add "CRITICAL: You MUST" language to the instruction

questions.why: Correcting over and over is a documented failure mode; the kitchen-sink session degrades recall as context grows (context rot).

questions.q: How should screenshots be arranged in a UX-critique prompt?

options.text: Text first, then images, so the model knows what to look for
Images before text, each labelled (e.g. "Image 1:") so you can reference them
One image per message, never more

questions.why: Text-before-image ordering produces weaker results; tiny or blurry screenshots are a documented error source.

questions.q: Which file type is not supported as an input at all?
questions.why: PPTX is an output type only — as are ZIP archives on the input side. XLSX reads reliably but requires code execution.

questions.q: Writing marketing copy and then translating it in a separate step is an example of which pattern?

options.text: Prompt chaining — Anthropic's own canonical example

questions.why: Generate-then-translate is the canonical chain; use evaluator-optimizer on top when you can score the asset against explicit criteria.

questions.q: You have legacy code that forces JSON by prefilling the assistant response. What happens on Claude 4.6+?

options.text: It still works but costs more
It returns a 400 error — migrate to Structured Outputs
It silently degrades to free-form text
It works only when tool_choice is set to any

questions.why: Prefilled responses are deprecated on 4.6+. Structured Outputs give a structural guarantee rather than a behavioral one.

questions.q: What is the just-in-time pattern for analyzing a large dataset in Claude Code?

options.text: Load the full CSV into context so nothing is missed
Write targeted queries, use head/tail and pandas to profile, and store intermediate results to files
Split the file into 200 chunks and paste them sequentially
Ask for estimates rather than computed aggregates

questions.why: Dumping whole datasets into the prompt causes context rot — and trusting aggregates that were never actually computed is the matching failure.

questions.q: What does legacy "CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool" language do on current models?
questions.why: Keep tool sets small and unambiguous instead: if a human engineer can't say which tool applies, an agent can't either.

questions.q: How is API usage billed relative to a Claude Pro or Enterprise subscription?

options.text: Subscription seats include an API token allowance
API billing is prepaid credits, completely separate from subscriptions
API usage is invoiced against the same seat contract
Enterprise seats grant unlimited API access

questions.why: A seat license buys you nothing at the API layer — credits are purchased in the Console.

questions.q: Which header carries an Anthropic API key?
questions.why: Bearer tokens are reserved for short-lived OAuth / Workload Identity Federation credentials. anthropic-version pins the API contract and must be sent explicitly.

questions.q: A response contains a tool call with an ID prefixed srvtoolu_. What do you do?

options.text: Execute it and return a tool_result
Nothing — Anthropic's infrastructure already ran it; never return a tool_result
Return an empty tool_result to acknowledge it

questions.why: toolu_ means your code must execute and return a result; srvtoolu_ is a server tool that already ran.

questions.q: What is the classic streaming bug the guide warns about?

options.text: Deltas can arrive out of order
Errors can arrive mid-stream after the connection already returned HTTP 200
message_start can fire more than once

questions.why: Status-code-only error handling misses in-stream error events like overloaded_error — always handle the error event itself.

questions.q: What are the prompt-caching token multipliers, and in what order does invalidation cascade?

options.text: Read 0.1×, 5-min write 1.25×, 1-hour write 2×; invalidation cascades tools → system → messages
Read 0.5×, write 1×; invalidation cascades messages → system → tools
Read free, write 2×; caches never invalidate within the TTL
Read 0.1×, write 1×; caches are shared across workspaces

questions.why: Any byte change in a prefix invalidates everything after it, and caches are scoped per workspace. Check usage for cache_read_input_tokens to confirm hits.

questions.q: What are the per-request PDF limits on the API, and what do you do beyond them?

options.text: 50 pages / 10 MB; split the document manually
100 pages / 32 MB; upload via the Files API and reference the file_id
There is no page limit, only a 32 MB size limit

questions.why: Claude reads both the text layer and page images, so scanned documents and charts come through — within those limits.

questions.q: What does the Message Batches API trade for its 50% discount?

options.text: Model quality — batches run on Haiku only
Latency and streaming; results arrive within 24 hours
Tool use, which is unavailable in batches
Prompt caching, which is disabled for batched requests

questions.why: Ideal for eval sweeps, backfills, and nightly enrichment. Expired requests are not billed, and results are retained 29 days.

questions.q: You send thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 8000} to Opus 4.7. What happens, and what is the current approach?

options.text: It works; adaptive thinking is opt-in
The request errors — use thinking: adaptive with output_config.effort instead
The budget is silently ignored and thinking is disabled
It works but thinking tokens are billed as input tokens

questions.why: Legacy budgets are unsupported on Opus 4.7 and later. Thinking tokens bill as output tokens either way, so effort is your cost/latency dial.

questions.q: What is the mental model for a 429 versus a 529?

options.text: 429 is the service's problem; 529 is yours
429 is your problem — slow down and honor the headers; 529 is Anthropic-wide capacity — back off with jitter
Both mean the request is malformed; do not retry

questions.why: Both are retryable, but for different reasons — and 529 can surface inside a 200-OK stream as an error event.

questions.q: How does the Claude Agent SDK differ from Claude Managed Agents?

options.text: The Agent SDK runs the agent loop in your process; Managed Agents is a hosted REST service priced per session-hour
They are the same product under two names
The Agent SDK is hosted; Managed Agents runs locally
The Agent SDK is TypeScript-only; Managed Agents is Python-only

questions.why: A single async query() replaces the manual tool loop and runs the built-in tools — in your process, against your files.

questions.q: Where do you enforce policy on an Agent SDK run?

options.text: In the system prompt, by describing the rules
In hooks — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit
In max_tokens, by bounding what the agent can do

questions.why: Hooks are in-process callbacks with matchers — your enforcement point, and where irreversible actions get gated.

questions.q: What is the Golden Rule of prompt clarity?

options.text: Every prompt should fit in 200 words
Show the prompt to a colleague with minimal context — if they would be confused, Claude will be too
Always include at least ten examples
State constraints as prohibitions so nothing is ambiguous

questions.why: Treat Claude as a brilliant but brand-new employee who lacks your norms and workflow context.

questions.q: What is the champion model for team adoption?

options.text: A mandate from leadership with a deadline
One credible practitioner per team who coaches peers by modelling real workflows
A vendor-delivered training day for the whole org
A centre of excellence that reviews every prompt

questions.why: Adoption spreads through people, not mandates — champions model workflows in shared Projects rather than delivering slide decks.

questions.q: Audit logs cover the past 180 days. What does that imply operationally?

options.text: Nothing — Anthropic archives older logs on request
Export on a schedule or stream via the Compliance API; do not discover the limit during an investigation
Retention controls extend audit-log life automatically
You should disable audit logging to save storage

questions.why: Logs expire; investigations start late. Scheduled export well inside the window is the governance checklist item.

questions.q: Which pairing of model and price is correct as of August 2026?

options.text: Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 per MTok and Opus 5 at $5/$25 per MTok

questions.why: Fable 5 sits at $10/$50, and Sonnet 5's introductory $2/$10 rises to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01 — verify before quoting.

questions.q: What token multipliers should you expect from agentic workloads?

options.text: Agents and chat are equivalent; only the model matters

questions.why: That is why the monthly cost review looks at Claude Code and agentic workflows separately from ordinary chat.

questions.q: What is the guide's working rule on sharing chats?

options.text: Never share a chat containing customer data, credentials, personal data, or pre-release information; review the whole thread first and prefer sharing a cleaned artifact
Only Owners may create share links
Publish artifacts instead of chats — published artifacts are always private

questions.why: Shared and published content propagates further than users expect — links get forwarded and remixes get published.

questions.q: Why does every shared project need a named knowledge owner?

options.text: To prune stale documents and resolve contradictions — Claude will try to follow contradictory instructions
To hold the Primary Owner role
To pay for the project's usage

questions.why: Document hygiene in Projects' RAG is more impactful than prompt tuning, and contradictions must be resolved rather than layered over.

questions.q: How should each item in Anthropic's monthly release notes be triaged?
questions.why: An assigned owner and a monthly review slot turn a monthly release cadence from a surprise into a process.

questions.q: What does every deprecation or model retirement need attached to it?

options.text: A migration owner and a deadline

questions.why: Organizations that skip this get surprised by removals like budget_tokens and prefill.

questions.q: What are MCP's three participants?

options.text: Host (the AI app), client (one per server, inside the host), and server (exposing tools, resources, prompts)

questions.why: The protocol splits into a JSON-RPC 2.0 data layer and a swappable transport layer, identical across transports.

questions.q: When is the stdio transport the right choice over Streamable HTTP?

options.text: For shared remote servers behind TLS serving many clients
For local filesystem, git, and shell tools with local credentials and exactly one client
For anything that needs horizontal scaling

questions.why: stdio launches the server as a local subprocess; Streamable HTTP is the single-endpoint transport for shared remote servers.

questions.q: What does domain capture do beyond routing logins through your SSO?

options.text: Deletes personal accounts on your domain
Pulls existing individual accounts on your domain into the managed workspace

questions.why: It solves shadow IT — which is why staff should be told before you flip it; their history moves into an org you administer.

questions.q: How do the four layers of the connector permission stack combine?

options.text: As a union — any layer that grants access grants it
As an intersection — removing access at any one layer removes it entirely
The Claude-side org policy overrides the other three
OAuth scopes override the source system's permissions

questions.why: Source-system permissions ∩ OAuth scopes ∩ MCP tool design ∩ Claude-side admin policy = what Claude can actually do.

questions.q: What distinguishes a subagent inside the agentic loop?

options.text: It shares the parent's context window to stay in sync
It has its own context window and tool set, attributed back via parent_tool_use_id
It can only run read-only tools

questions.why: You shape the loop from three directions — configuration (CLAUDE.md, permissionMode), the tool surface, and hooks — and delegate through subagents.

questions.q: Two governance properties of Projects matter for enterprises. Which pair is correct?

options.text: Cross-chat search and memory do not leak across project boundaries; sharing is role-based (Private / View / Edit)
Projects are always public to the org; artifacts are private to their creator
Memory is shared across all projects; sharing is all-or-nothing
Project knowledge is encrypted client-side; sharing requires an admin

questions.why: RAG retrieval assembles only the relevant passages per query, and artifacts are shared only among project members.
